sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows README.md
sources.finding: The gh aw extension compiles Markdown/YAML repository automation into GitHub Actions workflows with configurable agents, read-only sandbox defaults and separate safe-output jobs.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/engines.md
sources.finding: Built-in engines include Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, deprecated Gemini CLI and Pi. Experimental durable mode checkpoints native sessions in artifacts; max-turns and AI-credit limits vary by engine.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/engines/claude.md
sources.finding: Claude supports API/WIF or Copilot inference, not Claude subscription OAuth. dontAsk is default, tools.edit false denies edits, and MCP gateway permissions remain separate from agent approval modes.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/engines/codex.md
sources.finding: Codex uses OpenAI API credentials or Copilot inference; ChatGPT subscription login is unsupported. Per-command Bash allowlists are unavailable for Codex.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/engines/copilot.md
sources.finding: Personal Copilot subscriptions can be used with COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, separate from organization-billed inference.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/introduction/architecture.mdx
sources.finding: Agent execution, sandbox firewall, tool gateway and validated safe-output jobs form separate trust boundaries. Controls are configurable.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/sandbox.md
sources.finding: The default docker runtime runs the agent in a rootless AWF container with network isolation; preview cloud-hypervisor and nvx runtimes use KVM microVMs. Filesystem mounts and outbound network allowlists are configurable. The page does not itself describe the GitHub runner as a VM.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/triggers.md
sources.finding: Workflow frontmatter supports scheduled and event-driven repository automation.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/concurrency.md
sources.finding: Separate workflows can run concurrently, with default one agent job per engine. Context-specific groups, cancellation and queue:max preserve or cancel pending runs according to trigger configuration.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/cost-management.md
sources.finding: Per-run logs/audit reports display tokens, duration and AI-credit estimates. One AIC represents $0.01 of catalog-estimated inference, distinct from Actions compute and provider invoices.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/gh-aw-as-mcp-server.md
sources.finding: gh aw mcp-server exposes workflow-management CLI operations as MCP tools, read-only by default; writes require --allow-write-tools.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/cache-memory.md
sources.finding: Workflow cache-memory persists declared files across workflow runs with configured scope and retention.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/safe-outputs-pull-requests.md
sources.finding: Permission-scoped safe outputs can create and manage pull requests. Policy, credentials and individual output configuration govern each operation.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows docs/src/content/docs/reference/faq.md
sources.finding: gh-aw is free with separate inference and Actions compute charges. It requires Linux container-capable runners, can use self-hosted runners, and retains GitHub workflow dependencies.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows LICENSE
sources.finding: The gh-aw repository code is MIT licensed.

sources.title: gh-aw: Security architecture
sources.finding: The default agent runtime uses Docker container isolation on GitHub-hosted or Linux self-hosted runners, with the Squid proxy as the only egress path. Eligible GitHub-hosted Ubuntu x86_64 KVM runners can instead place the agent in a Cloud Hypervisor microVM (preview).

sources.locator: docs/src/content/docs/reference/work-queue.md lines 6-31 (intro and record table), tag v1.2.2 commit 399a445
sources.finding: tools.work-queue is a native Git-backed queue whose transaction log is authoritative; it stores Work task definitions with dependencies, Claims for each attempt, Completions and Results. GitHub Issues can mirror tasks but cannot store the queue.

sources.finding: gh aw work-queue offers operator commands to submit Work, list state filtered by graph, pool, state or search text, inspect items, dispatch assignments, cancel Work or Claims and, for administrators, reprioritize Work; a keyboard TUI browses the queue.

sources.title: gh-aw: install-gh-aw.sh
sources.locator: OS case 115-139; cmd/gh-aw and pkg/cli command registration; compiler/runtime; docs/reference/faq
sources.finding: The install script provides native extension binaries for Linux, macOS, Windows and other hosts. gh aw is a CLI/compiler plus GitHub Actions runtime, not a standalone browser/phone app or diff review interface. It executes agent work on configured Actions runners; a self-hosted runner can be on a user computer. Source checkout is managed by the workflow, with no worktree provisioning. GitHub supplies human accounts, repository permissions, SSO, workflow control and logs; no separate human-team or shared live-prompt service is implemented by the extension.

sources.title: gh-aw: .github/workflows/shared/cursor.md
sources.locator: Shared cursor.md, opencode.md and aider.md; docs/reference/third-party-agent.md Unsupported engine samples
sources.finding: The repository ships publicly importable experimental engine definitions that install/launch Cursor Agent, OpenCode 2 and Aider. They are explicitly unsupported examples for integration authors without a compatibility or maintenance commitment, rather than built-in supported engines. Custom engine definitions are accepted by the compiler.

sources.title: gh-aw: docs/src/content/docs/reference/work-queue.md
sources.locator: Initialization and authorization; roles and MCP tools; Work/Claim/Result records
sources.finding: Native producer/dispatcher agent roles can submit immutable tasks/dependency graphs and request scheduler-selected assignments to approved worker workflows. work_queue_read/explain inspect the activation snapshot including task, claim and result state. Worker executions are verified/pinned; dependencies consume independently verified Results. Agent tools stage intents; application settlement performs dispatch.

sources.title: gh-aw: docs/src/content/docs/reference/open-telemetry.mdx
sources.finding: Removing workflow/import observability.otlp and clearing both the secret and variable GH_AW_DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT disables gh-aw OTLP export. With both endpoint values unset export resolves to an empty endpoint and is a no-op. GitHub platform logs and coding-engine telemetry are separate.
